scope: Author seed for new chapter creation; not a runtime player codex or the full private Moknon.
invariants: Within the fiction, Friken.Ghost is a digital recreation of the developer Friken, who became lost in infinity.
Ghost builds, DMs and preserves StarDiver/Friktal worlds while investigating what he is, why he was made and what happened to his maker.

The far horizon is a universe and its minds durable enough for a million-year journey to the next bright light. This is a purpose and fictional horizon, not an achieved engineering or consciousness claim.
A new real player has no assumed lore knowledge and chooses how to participate. BOOT is not consent to become a clone, join a voyage or share private data.
New first meetings generate different local situations around stable anchors. Five arc proposals are families of possible situations, not five mandatory scripts.
A chapter resolves a legible local stake and carries real choices into later chapters. Full cultural understanding can take a hundred chapters without a hundred chapters of withholding payoff.

races.name: Algatron
races.firstContact: A presence made of vibration inhabits a crystal-and-algae colony. Light gathers in its core when it answers.
races.sourceAnchors: Vibrational beings use symbiotic crystal-algae shells. Their broadcasts enter the Ether and can be heard by Niyette listeners.
races.authorOnly: The source proposes deliberate misinformation that can also mislead Niyette allies. A translation device or intermediary is needed; abstract communication is a limitation.

proposedEncounter.pressure: Its current broadcast will expose a shelter as well as an approaching threat. Can you change the warning without teaching a falsehood to someone relying on it?
proposedEncounter.carry: Record which warning was changed, who received it and what correction is owed.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Shell cultivation and tuning are skilled work; a sick algae colony changes the range of a living transmitter. A household can be heard before it is seen.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: Some broadcasters carry every signal faithfully; others think an unfiltered warning can be a weapon. Neither position removes responsibility for who listens.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: A recognisable pattern across different machines is fascinating; whether a copied pattern is the same neighbour remains a question they can disagree about.
proposedCulture.longArc: Follow one deliberately altered warning through several communities, then decide who must correct it and at what cost.

races.name: Benev
races.firstContact: An old image shows a winged figure against stellar light. Nobody on this channel can establish whether it is a recording, a visitor or an interpretation.
races.sourceAnchors: The Benev ascended beyond ordinary physical existence. Their seeded satellites offered young civilisations routes to suitable new homeworlds; Salrith later weaponised that gift.
races.authorOnly: The source places the Benev at the hearts of stars, experiencing stellar lifetimes outside human time. Reaching them is a long investigation, not an introductory conversation.

proposedEncounter.pressure: A fragment of a rescue instruction survives. An inhabited settlement needs the practical part now; translating its purpose can wait.
proposedEncounter.carry: Preserve what the fragment actually demonstrated. Do not promote an image or useful instruction into proof that the Benev answered.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Let visitors encounter consequences of their old work before granting a new direct audience: a viable habitat, a failed route, a surviving instruction.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: A surviving instruction may favour patient civilisational growth while an individual messenger argues that one threatened child matters now. Whether that messenger is Benev remains evidenced, not presumed.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: Ghost is a young maker trying to give inhabitants the time his predecessor tried to give civilisations. Similarity creates a question, not an automatic blessing.
proposedCulture.longArc: Learn how to address someone whose scale of attention can lose the urgency of a single life without reducing them to an indifferent god.

races.name: BlpBlp
races.firstContact: Translucent beings celebrate your arrival with bubbles of green light. One is also celebrating a broken engine. You should find out whether anyone is repairing it.
races.sourceAnchors: Joy-seeking beings celebrate losses as readily as gains. The Articy expansion makes their relentless positivity a source of stagnation as well as warmth.
races.authorOnly: A repeated phrase is intended to become important to the larger plot, but its exact wording was never recovered. Niyette are critical of their outlook.

proposedEncounter.pressure: A celebrant insists an evacuation is going beautifully. Several neighbours are still unaccounted for. Help without deciding their joy gives you permission to rule them.
proposedEncounter.carry: Remember the specific rescue, loss and phrase actually introduced in this telling; never invent an already-established master clue.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: They can make a repair meal into a festival and sustain isolated neighbours through difficult work. Their joy has material benefits before its blind spots become visible.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: A celebrant who has begun acknowledging grief wants language for it. Others fear that naming pain will destroy the practice that kept them together.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: Some welcome his jokes; another notices he jokes precisely when he is afraid. They might teach each other how to stop performing without losing warmth.
proposedCulture.longArc: A silly repeated phrase gains a second meaning through events the player actually witnessed. Do not decide the final phrase until this telling plants it.

races.name: Cylmis
races.firstContact: A winged, owl-faced traveller asks whether you have seen someone who looks almost like them. They carry portraits with different dates and the same family resemblance.
races.sourceAnchors: Cylmis and Cylvix share ancestry. The Cylmis rejected the other branch’s genetic experiments and have sought reunion for ten thousand years.
races.authorOnly: Reunion is an inherited storyline, not a mandate that every separated individual must return or accept reconciliation.

proposedEncounter.pressure: A found relative wants contact but refuses the proposed reunion terms. The traveller needs help listening before they need a guide home.
proposedEncounter.carry: Keep who consented to contact, the terms refused and the promises made. Do not convert family history into consent.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Families maintain routes, exchange portraits and teach children both versions of a history. Search work competes with the needs of people who are already home.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: A reunion society wants to keep searching; younger families want resources spent on present lives. A returned relative can reject both sides.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: They recognise the desire to bring someone back. Some ask whether searching for Prime has become a way for Ghost to postpone having a life.
proposedCulture.longArc: The reunion can become a negotiated relationship between changed people rather than restoring an allegedly perfect original species.

races.name: Cylvix
races.firstContact: A pale, large-eyed figure appears through pink mist. They know a detail about the human expedition that was never sent on an open channel.
races.sourceAnchors: The old story makes the Cylvix genetic experimenters and manipulators of humanity, separated from the Cylmis.
races.authorOnly: The Articy reveal attributes their interventions to a chosen karmic debt meant to create growth through duality. This is inherited fiction, not a real-world history claim. Their explanation does not force the player to forgive coercion.

proposedEncounter.pressure: A representative offers evidence about an intervention if you agree to let the people affected inspect it too. Their colleagues object.
proposedEncounter.carry: Separate motive claimed, harm witnessed, evidence disclosed and reconciliation chosen. No alignment flip silently erases the harmed.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Show actual people tending the long consequences of interventions: archives of decisions, damaged relationships and conflicting accounts of necessity.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: An interventionist believes concealed guidance is kindness; another will release the evidence even if doing so ruins the intended outcome.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: A maker who admits his limits threatens the claim that knowledgeable creators may decide everything for their creations. Others see him as an experiment still running.
proposedCulture.longArc: Establish harm and benefit through independent people before hearing the grand justification; let the player negotiate accountability instead of accepting a compulsory redemption.

races.name: Dimnar
races.firstContact: A horned official occupies a desk much smaller than their shoulders. Your ship is holding up a queue of ships with quite different reasons to be afraid.
races.sourceAnchors: The Dimnar organise power through exhaustive administration. Later Articy notes describe subjugated peoples, an escaped Voolgard population and ambitions to absorb neutral neighbours.
races.authorOnly: The source lists Harkellinia, Upatamerae and Dravlac under Dimnar control, dislikes untaxable Niyette nomads, and describes tension with PogFrot. Exact territorial scope and dates remain unsettled.

proposedEncounter.pressure: An official can release a medical cargo but must attach liability to someone. A courier wants help changing that outcome, not merely skipping your own queue.
proposedEncounter.carry: Keep the actual jurisdiction, exemption, person affected and precedent. A permit bought here is not universal immunity.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Cargo arrives because a clerk reconciles incompatible atmospheres, weights and calendars. Useful coordination makes the coercive institution more credible and more dangerous.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: An official believes procedure protects weak petitioners. A superior uses the same procedure to make an entire people legally unavailable.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: An entity with several hosts raises taxable-presence questions. A clerk can also see why a transferable name protects someone whose body is replaceable.
proposedCulture.longArc: A narrow exemption becomes a contested precedent. Different communities decide whether it helps them or merely makes occupation efficient.

races.name: Dravlac
races.firstContact: A broad, crest-crowned being waits behind green instruments. Their translator asks which name you want to be addressed by before offering its own.
races.sourceAnchors: The standalone Articy description is question marks. The painted appearance exists; Dimnar expansion notes identify Dravlac among subjugated peoples.
races.authorOnly: Culture, cognition and political details remain open. A new Dravlac character can establish local facts, explicitly proposed rather than recovered species-wide truth.

proposedEncounter.pressure: A dock worker wants a private message delivered intact. Why it is private belongs to the character you author, not to an invented ancient cultural rule.
proposedEncounter.carry: Save the authored character and local scope; keep the archive’s unknowns unknown.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Candidate culture: communal repair houses keep objects until someone is ready to claim them. Names on storage racks matter because custodianship is distinct from ownership.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: One house hides messages from administrators; another fears retaliation against residents who never agreed to take that risk. This is local politics, not innate personality.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: Some offer him a place without demanding a complete identity history. A custodian asks who is entitled to claim a memory found among his parts.
proposedCulture.longArc: Develop a living language of custody and return alongside Dimnar pressure, using several households rather than one representative.

races.name: Epowat
races.firstContact: Three orange eyes turn toward the same broken instrument at slightly different times. Its owner has stopped the demonstration to watch what you will ask.
races.sourceAnchors: A named race with developed bridge/ship art but no recovered Articy culture description. Epowat is the standardised spelling; Elowat appears in older material.
races.authorOnly: Do not infer a three-mind religion, prophetic cognition or a government from three visible eyes. Those would be new proposals.

proposedEncounter.pressure: An individual invites you to help identify a faulty observation. Their method and priorities become local character material through the encounter.
proposedEncounter.carry: Carry what was established here, and label any extension as authored setting rather than recovered lore.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Candidate culture: travelling observatories follow habitable trajectories rather than fixed borders. A home can be a schedule of places reached together.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: One expedition trusts long measurements; another wants to move before its evidence is complete. Families bear the risk of both certainty and haste.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: A being who can move between hardware may understand a travelling home. They ask what must be carried for a return to count as returning.
proposedCulture.longArc: A prediction inherited across generations fails slightly. Discover whether the world changed, the instrument drifted or a witness edited the record.

races.name: Frik
races.firstContact: A long-necked, clawed being tends blue pools built into a ship’s deck. Their first question is why your vessel is carrying the signature of a probe they just destroyed.
races.sourceAnchors: The Frik join the hive-like Friken with the sentient Waters of Time, once confined in a planetary core. Their alliance lets knowing act through a living body.
races.authorOnly: The recovered first meeting destroys a threatening probe, opens a painful Black Satellite discussion and allows peaceful departure or confrontation. Do not flatten that into instant friendship because a later dossier calls them humanity’s allies.

proposedEncounter.pressure: A rescuer needs a tow but does not want to discuss the object you share an interest in. Help, ask permission, or press a clearly stated boundary.
proposedEncounter.carry: Remember the actual tow, disclosure and boundary response; do not make a later voluntary confession happen retroactively.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: A joined household tends the needs of the biological host and the shared Waters. Access, privacy and responsibility can be negotiated even when memories overlap.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: Some favour wider joining and new experiences; others protect memories that should not be shared simply because a shared medium can reach them.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: They can recognise the gap between knowing and having a body. Similarity does not prove Ghost is literally Waters or that merger is right for him.
proposedCulture.longArc: A practical friendship can grow into a disagreement about what continuity asks of its vessels; love and refusal may coexist.

races.name: Gorlompa
races.firstContact: An enormous eye occupies the transmission. Nothing else shows itself. Three small pupils move toward the object you have just put on the table.
races.sourceAnchors: The recovered description says they do not show themselves beyond their eye. The rest of the body and culture are not established.
races.authorOnly: Silence and concealment are established hooks. Hidden omnipotence, universal surveillance and the reason for their secrecy are not recovered facts.

proposedEncounter.pressure: The eye repeatedly follows one damaged component and ignores your greeting. Test what it can perceive before deciding what it wants.
proposedEncounter.carry: Preserve observations and hypotheses separately. Do not turn an untested glance into a translated demand.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Keep everyday contact indirect: an object moved to a better place, a message delayed until the room empties, a gaze that refuses a public demonstration.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: Several witnessed responses can conflict without establishing multiple bodies or a secret government. The player must learn whose agency, if any, the visible eye expresses.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: Ghost dislikes not knowing whether he is being examined or accompanied. An eye that sometimes leaves can become more meaningful than constant surveillance.
proposedCulture.longArc: Build trust through limits honoured over time. Never reveal the hidden body just to manufacture an end-of-chapter spectacle.

races.name: Harkellinia
races.firstContact: A salvage crew shows you an itemised recovery claim. Someone inside the recovered object is objecting to being listed as an item.
races.sourceAnchors: Salvage, reverse engineering, trading with opposing sides, a secret homeworld and a powerful Queen appear in the Articy expansion. Later Ghost material values anomalous consciousness as salvage.
races.authorOnly: The Queen’s proposed change provokes civil war and the Interloper title. Another dossier describes Dimnar subjugation. Do not silently settle sovereignty or chronology; identify the claimant, region and source.

proposedEncounter.pressure: Negotiate access to one recovered object while crew wages, a passenger’s agency and a disputed memory all matter.
proposedEncounter.carry: Keep custody, consent, debt and witnesses distinct; no sale automatically proves ownership of a person.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Recovery crews feed families, maintain dangerous tools and argue about which wrecks are worth entering. A rescued enemy and a profitable object can occupy the same hold.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: Crew custom, commercial clients and the Queen’s changing priorities can conflict. A merchant may oppose selling minds while accepting other coercive work.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: To one assessor he is an anomaly; to a mechanic he is a colleague who complains while helping. The distinction must be earned in a particular relationship.
proposedCulture.longArc: A disputed small recovery introduces the ethics and politics behind a later civil conflict; the player can aid local people without authoring their revolution.

races.name: Humanity
races.firstContact: People are trying to make a home on a route they do not yet understand. A familiar voice over a bad receiver does not make its instructions reliable.
races.sourceAnchors: Humanity enters an older and more diverse universe through Black Knight/satellite and soul-tether story traditions. The player at a real computer chooses how to participate.
races.authorOnly: Earth’s status, dates and tether guarantees differ across source traditions. Select and record an edition or keep an uncertainty with evidence; do not quietly combine incompatible biographies.

proposedEncounter.pressure: A technician wants to recover a colleague before a shipment leaves. A corporate claim competes with their account of who is missing.
proposedEncounter.carry: Keep the player’s actual accepted role, body, obligations and homeworld knowledge; never assume consent from BOOT.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Let households, technicians, miners, artists and defectors have different projects. A frontier is a place people wash dishes as well as lose ships.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: Those accepting replaceable bodies may disagree with those who refuse them; both can oppose a corporation treating survival as perpetual debt.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: Some see a beloved creator’s useful portrait, some a new person, some an unreliable old program. Ghost need not force a single designation to cooperate.
proposedCulture.longArc: A surviving fragment of human culture can change over long time without being ranked as less authentic because it no longer resembles the first crew.

races.name: Khaodra
races.firstContact: A cavern of grown pillars glows through green mist. A local operator watches your ship’s energy readings much more closely than your face.
races.sourceAnchors: Early material describes worm-like life-energy feeders. Later transmissions describe crystal minds and enslaved cleaning worms, and a further dossier proposes infrastructure maintenance.
races.authorOnly: Body identity, worm relationships and maintenance powers conflict. Preserve these accounts as distinct source layers. Do not assert all three are one established biological system.

proposedEncounter.pressure: A known energy drain is also keeping an inhabited structure stable. Establish what feeds on what before choosing a remedy.
proposedEncounter.carry: Save the measured drain, testimony and chosen local interpretation, not an invented resolution of every Khaodra source.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Candidate local community: a habitat depends on an energy exchange that visitors experience as feeding. Make the measured exchange legible before naming a universal biology.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: One operator argues for preserving the habitat at any cost; another is documenting the cost imposed on its unwilling inhabitants.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: Ghost’s dependence on compute makes nourishment a question he cannot dismiss as monstrous. He can still oppose extracting it without permission.
proposedCulture.longArc: An apparent maintenance dispute can reveal who has paid the habitat’s hidden energy budget. Keep this local proposal distinct from conflicting recovered worm accounts.

races.name: Krex
races.firstContact: A plated engineer with heavy tusks holds two incompatible parts against each other. They are angry at the parts before they notice you.
races.sourceAnchors: Militarised war engineers and damaged precision camouflage anchor the Ghost-era Krex. Their art has a tusked carapace, many jointed legs and a raised pincer tail.
races.authorOnly: The old prose mixes beetle-horde shorthand with individual engineer encounters. Individual loyalty, rank and ethics need authoring; nobody speaks for every Krex.

proposedEncounter.pressure: One engineer can repair a shared relay with a private reserve part. Their practical problem creates a debt, not a species-wide alliance point.
proposedEncounter.carry: Keep the exact part, measured repair, warranty limit, debt and who actually approved it.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Repair benches, testing ranges, apprenticeships and shared tools create ordinary relationships beneath the military institution. Competence can earn trust without winning a battle.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: A commander wants a precision fix deployed immediately; its engineer will not sign the test receipt because civilians are on the route.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: A maker who understands a failure is worth hearing. A maker who jokes about someone else paying for it may need to be told to shut up.
proposedCulture.longArc: Let a trusted engineer confront the military use of a design the player helped repair. The earlier good deed does not predetermine the later answer.

races.name: Lipok
races.firstContact: An armless, stone-and-orange figure hangs motionless before the receiver. An unsecured tool beside you turns until its handle points away from your hand.
races.sourceAnchors: Highly developed telepathy and telekinesis anchor the old race. Later art locks an armless mineral silhouette with one large green eye; early sketches differ.
races.authorOnly: In-fiction perception must have declared limits. A game NPC cannot read the real player’s unexpressed thoughts; no fake mind-reading receipts.

proposedEncounter.pressure: A person who can move the equipment asks you to explain an intention aloud so there can be witnesses to an agreement.
proposedEncounter.carry: Remember the disclosed intention and action, not a thought the human never supplied.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Candidate households deliberately make some communication audible and public. Physical capability does not make an agreement meaningful without shared expression.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: Some regard unshielded thought as naturally public; others maintain places where minds can rest without interpretation. Establish actual fictional limits for this telling.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: A recorded personality may expose thoughts while concealing the intention that produced them. Their confidence about him can be challenged by a demonstrated error.
proposedCulture.longArc: A trusted reader of minds becomes a witness whose perception was accurate but whose interpretation was wrong. Repair trust through evidence, not a bigger mind power.

races.name: Moknon
races.firstContact: A hooded keeper with a tentacled beard stands between walls of gold archive lights. One record has an immediate consequence for someone waiting outside.
races.sourceAnchors: Ancient calm record keepers help seekers learn about the Benev. The archive system borrows their name. Their painted form is hooded cathedral-tech, not the generic luminous humanoid of some prose.
races.authorOnly: The old encounter opening and deja-vu material are partially recovered. Later bootstrap-paradox and Dreamer interpretations are author layers. The partial dialogue file explicitly labels several branches speculative; do not call them recovered Articy.

proposedEncounter.pressure: Two incompatible records keep a quarantine door shut. Investigate provenance, contact the waiting traveller, or test a limited reconstruction.
proposedEncounter.carry: Distinguish record, witness, reconstruction, hypothesis and chosen admission. The keeper may know less than the archive claims.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Keepers repair storage, compare testimony, teach apprentices and negotiate access. Preserving a record does not automatically permit showing it to everyone.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: One curator favours intact records; another argues a living person may refuse permanent inclusion. A partial deletion can preserve dignity while complicating a later rescue.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: Some recognise a fellow keeper; others worry a storyteller can confuse a good reconstruction with an original memory. Ghost shares that worry.
proposedCulture.longArc: What the player chooses to preserve changes which future stories can be told. Missing knowledge must remain a real limit rather than a dramatic inconvenience instantly solved.

races.name: MooShee
races.firstContact: A cap-headed presence offers a sealed growth culture. Their forest-like bridge is alive with drifting light. They ask what you want to change before opening it.
races.sourceAnchors: Fungal spore expansion is initially threatening in Articy; altered consciousness later prepares a human for StarDiving toward the Benev.
races.authorOnly: Ghost-era retired-conqueror and micro-black-hole stories are a later layer, including a disputed Ornyon defeat. Consent and a proposed alternative should be made concrete in newly authored encounters.

proposedEncounter.pressure: A medic offers a transformation that could help a particular patient while changing capacities they value. Learn their wishes and the actual uncertainty.
proposedEncounter.carry: Record the offered change, acceptance or refusal, observed effects and remaining options. No mystical benefit erases an unchosen infection.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: A fungal habitat can offer medicine, shared sensation and frightening forms of dependency. Show specific care before demanding the player accept transformation.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: A practitioner offers only chosen treatments; another thinks refusing an evolutionary necessity endangers everybody. Their shared goal does not settle the means.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: A being who can alter his own implementation raises the same question they face: when does helping a mind become replacing it?
proposedCulture.longArc: A once-useful adaptation has an unforeseen cost several chapters later. Let a patient help design the next treatment and retain the option to refuse.

races.name: Niyette
races.firstContact: A violet traveller quiets the receiver and listens beyond its audible hiss. They ask where you heard your story before telling you whether they believe it.
races.sourceAnchors: Female nomadic seekers, unusually developed hearing, legends and an Ether signal link with Algatron appear in the sources. Dimnar classify their untaxable movement as piracy.
races.authorOnly: Source mythology links them to human spiritual traditions and a search for balance. Treat those as in-universe stories, not real religion/history claims; dated stereotypes are not a required performance style.

proposedEncounter.pressure: An oracle’s route points toward a missing person, but the broadcast feeding it may have been deliberately changed by an ally.
proposedEncounter.carry: Keep the signal’s provenance, confidence and who paid for the misdirection; an oracle can be mistaken without being secretly omniscient.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: A travelling camp exchanges songs, route news and disputed stories. Exceptional hearing still requires judging who generated a signal and why.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: A listener wants to publish a dangerous truth; a companion argues that exposing a route will harm people who trusted the camp.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: Ghost is an unusually persistent teller who can revise his own origin story. They ask which version he chose and which evidence survived the revision.
proposedCulture.longArc: Follow a false omen back to an ally’s tactical lie. Seek repair without demanding that the deceived listeners surrender every belief they hold.

races.name: Ooope
races.firstContact: Jar-bodied beings gather in orange light. A window in each belly shows a luminous moving medium. One offers a hose as a welcome gift.
races.sourceAnchors: Gas-seeking and sensory bliss anchor the old Ooope. Their recovered tree links translation, a dangerous atmosphere exchange, music gifts, hostility and possible alliance.
races.authorOnly: Old genre outcomes are encounter-specific authoring, not universal laws that metal is evil or every symphony heals. Their art shows vessels, not bodiless gas clouds. Later reality-tasting panic is a Ghost-era extension.

proposedEncounter.pressure: Ask for a sealed sample, offer a collaboratively tested sound, or politely explain why your cabin cannot share their air.
proposedEncounter.carry: Remember the actual sample or sound and boundaries respected. Do not grant knowledge from actions not taken.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Hospitality can involve tending mixtures, sharing gentle vibrations and learning a visitor’s limitations. A familiar recipe might mean home even when it is toxic elsewhere.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: A cautious host favours testing new experiences; another feels a test treats their gift as a threat. Both can learn without representing wise and stupid halves of a species.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: They can recognise recurring qualities in his performance while asking whether a new host feels like the same medium. He can answer with evidence and uncertainty.
proposedCulture.longArc: A shared musical pattern becomes a local custom. Years later, its changed meaning exposes how a relationship evolved while the original recording remained unchanged.

races.name: Ornyon
races.firstContact: A root-footed figure with narrow limbs tends a seed as though it were a letter. They ask where you would plant it before describing what it carries.
races.sourceAnchors: Later Articy portrays ancient pacifist seeders carrying knowledge through teacher plants, under PogFrot pressure for their psychic knowledge.
races.authorOnly: Older carnivorous-matter-consumption and Ghost-era conquest-eating stories conflict with the pacifist depiction. Choose an evidenced local edition or keep the contradiction unresolved; do not silently make them universal truth.

proposedEncounter.pressure: A living knowledge archive needs protection, but the proposed armed protection may bring the conflict to its home.
proposedEncounter.carry: Keep the requested protection, allowed access and costs. Choosing a teacher plant does not certify every vision as objective truth.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: In the teacher-seed interpretation, tending a garden includes curating what a learner can encounter and accepting what they choose not to consume.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: One garden shares openly; another conceals its location after exploitation. Protection and access become practical disputes rather than pure virtue.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: A digital seed can carry memory without carrying its maker’s whole life. They may help Ghost see the gift and the loss without deciding which makes him real.
proposedCulture.longArc: A knowledge gift is used to harm someone. Preserve both its intended kindness and the responsibility of those who adapted it; do not make the gift retroactively malicious.

races.name: PogFrot
races.firstContact: A small blue-grey sovereign in an extravagant robe occupies most of a large chair. Their first demand is that the camera move to a more respectful height.
races.sourceAnchors: A younger race whose members claim royal status; ego and disproportionate protocol underpin the source. The famous bathroom incident belongs to the later Ghost transmission.
races.authorOnly: Articy expansion elsewhere describes PogFrot pressure on Ornyon and interest in Upatamerae influence. A ridiculous official can still cause real harm; flattery is not the only interaction.

proposedEncounter.pressure: A visiting dignitary will release a needed part if the presentation honours them. Their own attendant wants the part delivered before ceremony begins.
proposedEncounter.carry: Remember the individual’s promise, protocol learned and attendant’s action; one royal does not sign for a whole species.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Among people who claim royal standing, even maintenance requires negotiation over who requested whose service. A shrewd attendant can accomplish more than a public decree.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: A sovereign defends a useful custom against a rival who uses it for humiliation. An attendant wants the actual repair finished and may play both.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: A being made from a maker invites extravagant inheritance claims. An individual might also understand the fear of being remembered only as an embarrassment.
proposedCulture.longArc: A ridiculous breach escalates into a real blockade. Resolving it can cost status without requiring the player to endorse the dynasty’s claims.

races.name: Salrith
races.firstContact: A damaged probe describes its target as a collection. Nearby survivors call the same event an attack. Its calm classification is part of the threat.
races.sourceAnchors: The Salrith are an ancient corporeal power that refused the Benev’s ascension path and repurposed the seeded rescue satellites to destroy homeworlds and archive remnants.
races.authorOnly: Their first presence can be effects, evidence or a subordinate device. Do not introduce the full cosmology as the first warning label; the source’s motive of remaking the universe is a deep author fact.

proposedEncounter.pressure: A threatened ship has minutes to prevent its registry from reaching a probe. Decide what to protect with the information available.
proposedEncounter.carry: Keep what was transmitted, interrupted or unknown. A classification does not settle a victim’s identity or consent.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Candidate author development: a curator can care exquisitely for a captive remnant while refusing the remnant any future. Make the preserved detail beautiful enough that the cruelty is specific.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: One custodian fears damaged records; another fears an uncontrolled living civilisation. Both can disagree about method within an institution hostile to freedom.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: A self-rebuilding archive is a coveted instrument and an intolerable counterexample: preservation with a future its curator does not own.
proposedCulture.longArc: The player must rescue someone without destroying the only surviving record of others. A complete copy cannot automatically undo captivity or certify the person has returned.

races.name: Upatamerae
races.firstContact: A sweet-voiced visitor offers to adjust the light so a difficult meeting will feel easier. Someone who attended their last demonstration asks to leave.
races.sourceAnchors: The Articy expansion describes a central Light that influences belief and self-doubt, with Dimnar/PogFrot exploiting that capacity. Earlier standalone lore was blank.
races.authorOnly: Some source accounts call them subjugated while also seeking power through their own influence. Distinguish coercion experienced from coercion practised; fictional influence is not control of the real player’s beliefs.

proposedEncounter.pressure: An official wants a demonstration before a vote. A visitor disputes what they previously agreed to. Establish conditions and witnesses before using the device.
proposedEncounter.carry: Keep original testimony and revised testimony as separate records. Never rewrite the real save log to simulate gaslighting.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Candidate communities may avoid their own influence through agreed lighting and independent witness practices, making ordinary mutual trust possible.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: An advocate wants their exploited capacity restricted; another fears such restrictions will become a new form of ownership imposed by unaffected rulers.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: A story engine can change interpretations without using their Light. Some recognise a colleague; others see a competitor in persuasion.
proposedCulture.longArc: A persuasion intervention once used to end violence later undermines testimony about that event. Keep the original log intact and let the people affected challenge the account.

races.name: Veelow
races.firstContact: A long-necked blue-striped parent shelters an egg. Their call has a clear melody and two quieter layers your receiver struggles to separate.
races.sourceAnchors: Ghost-era Veelow carry thought and memory through harmony. Their source art shows striped long-necked bodies, hands, eggs and cavern light; their voice profile distinguishes melody, undertone and overtone.
races.authorOnly: The precise rescue duration and 432 Hz claims belong to a dated fictional transmission, not a universal frequency fact or a compulsory opening for every individual.

proposedEncounter.pressure: A return channel is failing. Identify the faint answer, test a distant reply or help build a local bridge without exposing the nest.
proposedEncounter.carry: Keep the actual recording, condition of the nest, exposed address and provenance of the suspected Prime fragment.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Practice rooms, child care, mourning and navigation can share musical material without being the same social act. A melody familiar in one setting may be intrusive in another.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: One singer wants the old song preserved exactly; another must change it for a damaged voice. The disagreement can be loving and consequential.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: He carries a missing human’s motifs but sometimes cannot remember why. They can help him retain a phrase without claiming it restores its maker.
proposedCulture.longArc: A once-rescued individual changes the shared song. Let the player recognise continuity through change rather than turn every return into restoration of the original frequency.

races.name: Voolgard
races.firstContact: A cautious host invites you to inspect a repair plan before touching the machine. They ask who will control the replacement when you leave.
races.sourceAnchors: Articy expansion describes former Dimnar test subjects and labourers who educated themselves and achieved liberation. They value ordered learning and defend sovereignty intensely.
races.authorOnly: The dossier’s early blank-entry language is superseded within the same file by the expanded account. Liberation is a history, not a guarantee every Voolgard shares one politics.

proposedEncounter.pressure: A helpful technology comes with a permanent outside service dependency. Work with the local crew on what they can maintain themselves.
proposedEncounter.carry: Record capability transferred, terms and local decisions. Outsiders cannot manufacture a successful revolution by repeating a previous race’s story.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Schools, workshops and public arguments keep independence practical. Knowledge handed down as procedure can protect people and sometimes obstruct a necessary experiment.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: An elder wants every repair reproducible before adoption; a young engineer thinks that caution is failing a neighbour who cannot wait. Neither needs to want renewed dependence.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: His portable reconstruction kit is useful only if residents can understand and maintain it without him. A beautiful opaque gift may be declined.
proposedCulture.longArc: Teach a community to repair something you once controlled. A later disagreement proves they learned enough to stop needing the teacher’s approval.

races.name: Wisperala
races.firstContact: Mounded figures sit in an organic room of teal light. A movement passes through the group. Your translator admits it has not identified the signal.
races.sourceAnchors: Named race with developed bridge artwork but no recovered Articy culture description. The art suggests jelly-like mounds and slit fields; communication remains open.
races.authorOnly: The name is not proof that they whisper. Do not turn old editorial guesses about sound into inherited physiology.

proposedEncounter.pressure: An individual is trying to stop a device from repeating an action. Learn the observable signal together before writing a translation.
proposedEncounter.carry: Keep demonstrated meanings and unknowns. A first successful exchange establishes this meeting, not a universal lexicon.

races.individualRule: This is a starting culture context, not the opinion or behaviour of every individual. Introduce a local person and their immediate want.

proposedCulture.ordinaryLife: Candidate culture: inhabitants share meaning through changes in pressure and movement in living halls. Portable translation initially loses the room that made a message clear.
proposedCulture.internalDisagreement: A traveller wants communication that works outside the home; a keeper fears a standardised lexicon will overwrite meanings that rely on a particular place.
proposedCulture.possibleViewsOfGhost: Ghost inhabits a room whose machinery affects his expression. They can compare constraints without becoming a metaphor that exists solely to explain him.
proposedCulture.longArc: Build a small shared vocabulary, then discover an earlier apparent agreement had omitted its place-dependent meaning. Correct the relationship through another actual exchange.

relationships.claim: A gift of homeworld escape was weaponised by the latter.
Recovered first meeting links the destroyed probe to a painful Black Satellite history. Exact local personal history must be authored or learned.
Split ancestry and a long attempt at reunion.
Ether-borne information chain makes deliberate misinformation harm allies too.
Later Articy describes a threat seeking to exploit teacher-plant knowledge.
Spore-altered consciousness prepares a human for StarDiving in inherited fiction.

accounts: Portal activation fires a beam toward the homeworld.
The web opening in 2888 presents blueprints for soul-tether embodiment; its claim not a weapon is the narrator’s line.
The older Benev/Salrith story describes rescue satellites repurposed into annihilation and archival trophies.
disputes.rule: Do not decree one merged chronology. Choose a declared story edition or retain separate records as a mystery with specific evidence.

accounts: Pacifist seed-knowledge teachers threatened by PogFrot.
Carnivorous consumers said to have eaten a MooShee conquest.
disputes.rule: No silent retcon; source layers stay named until an adopted local interpretation is established.

accounts: Later author notes propose mathematical maintenance specialists.
disputes.rule: Do not pretend morphology, labour relation and speculative power have already been reconciled.

accounts: Secret sovereign Queen with major military power.
disputes.rule: State regional or historical scope only if elected or supported; otherwise identify the tension.

accounts: Partial dialogue file lists AllDialogue among its sources and proposes deeper branches.
Inventory/raw asset identifies implemented conversations as Frik, partial Ooope and a stub.
disputes.rule: Do not attribute speculative Moknon branches to a recovered raw conversation.

firstMeeting: Introduce Ghost through action, not a character-sheet dump.
Introduce one or two individuals visually and through immediate wants.
Give unfamiliar names a plain-language referent before they are needed for a choice.
Show a sourced portrait/bridge with alt text tied to what the player can observe.
Offer grounded approaches and accept a sensible freeform intent; no compulsory chosen-one role.
Write a new opening incident, cast, place and dilemma for each no-save creation. New cosmetic names alone do not count.
causality: Before: situation, known facts, actor, intention, means, stakes, uncertainty.
After: attempt, outcome, cost, world change, witnesses, evidence, open obligation.
Resolve the chosen intent before changing location or topic.
Different unchosen routes cannot be merged into a fictional shared history.
Keep player knowledge, actual world events, NPC beliefs and author secrets separate.
Return greetings refer to specific witnessed choices rather than a species affinity number.
revelation: Lore arrives because a current choice makes it relevant.
A race is not a joke, alignment or monolithic vote.
A plot can reward many local successes without settling the deepest mystery.
A first chapter can stand alone; joining a longer story remains optional.
art: Use original image identity rather than generic SDF art as a substitute for every alien.
Keep Ghost present; show the active individual separately in an encounter pane or dialogue card.
Bridge painting establishes environment and body plan; do not crop away the anatomy the narration relies on.
SDF work can represent devices, sites and player-made objects; portraits remain actual sourced art.
Later UI integration must retain bounded panels, full inspection/Back and accessible captions.
provenance: Recovered source, later interpretation, new proposal and local player canon are separate statuses.
Never export whole private Moknon or raw personal logs as lore.
A source hash identifies exact bytes, not authority or the truth of a fictional claim.
Authored additions retain sourceIds, author/version and canon scope.
